lines.trans: Have you heard, our owner is dying.
If I hear one more time that you are spreading gossip...
I will fire you that very same day!
Honestly, I am not spreading gossip.
That is all, go work calmly and do not cry.
Why are you gloomier than a storm cloud today?
They say our Eleonora Andreyevna is dying soon.
And Mikhail Dzhekovich almost fired me for it.
Wait, what do you mean Eleonora is dying?
She is very seriously ill, everyone already knows.
Where on earth did you get all of this?
Viktor Petrovich himself told us this morning.

examples.text: Конечно, я знаю, что там готовить.
examples.trans: Of course I know what there is to cook.

examples.text: Если останешься жив, признаю, что ты лучше.
examples.trans: If you stay alive, I will admit you are better.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'куда').

examples.text: Скажи, а откуда ты про это узнал?
examples.trans: Tell me, how did you find out about that?

examples.text: Откуда вы вообще всё это взяли?
examples.trans: Where on earth did you get all of this?

examples.text: Откуда у нас в ресторане рыба фугу?
examples.trans: Where did fugu fish come from in our restaurant?

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'обще').

examples.text: Вообще-то, шеф, мой паштет критику понравился.
examples.trans: Actually, Chef, the critic liked my pâté.

examples.text: Откуда вы вообще всё это взяли?
examples.trans: Where on earth did you get all of this?

examples.text: Так, ребята, меня тут вообще не было.
examples.trans: Alright, guys, I was never here at all.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'took, arrested', paired with 'брать'.

examples.text: Откуда вы вообще всё это взяли?
examples.trans: Where on earth did you get all of this?

examples.text: Возьмите на работу Галилея.
examples.trans: Go and hire Galileo.

examples.text: Возьми деньги.
examples.trans: Take the money.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'us', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Сегодня самый лучший день в моей жизни.
examples.trans: Today is the very best day of my life.

examples.text: А мы все уже думали, вы ушли.
examples.trans: And all of us already thought you had left.

examples.text: Мы очень рады снова видеть вас, шеф.
examples.trans: We are very glad to see you again, Chef.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'in the morning' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Нам утром сам Виктор Петрович рассказал.
examples.trans: Viktor Petrovich himself told us this morning.

examples.text: Доброе утро!
examples.trans: Good morning!

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро!
examples.trans: What a lovely morning!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'yourself', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Сегодня самый лучший день в моей жизни.
examples.trans: Today is the very best day of my life.

examples.text: На самом деле там неустойка по договору.
examples.trans: In reality there is a penalty clause in the contract.

examples.text: Я его с самого детства обожаю.
examples.trans: I have adored it since early childhood.

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'сказать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'told', paired with 'рассказывать'.

examples.text: Нам утром сам Виктор Петрович рассказал.
examples.trans: Viktor Petrovich himself told us this morning.

examples.text: Расскажи, что случилось.
examples.trans: Tell me what happened.

examples.text: Я всё расскажу маме.
examples.trans: I'll tell Mum everything.
